oneLine: Flipkart employees seek fair ESOP treatment ahead of IPO, with potential buybacks worth Rs 38,000 crore.

sources.title: Flipkart employees press Walmart for ‘fair’ ESOP treatment ahead of IPO: Report
Ex-Flipkart Executives press Walmart to buy out their stock options
Flipkart said to weigh $2 bn Esop buyout for current employees in early 2027 amid IPO uncertainty

synopsis: Flipkart employees have approached parent company Walmart's board seeking fair and equitable treatment for their vested ESOPs ahead of a planned IPO. A group of at least eight former Flipkart CXOs and senior executives wrote an email to Walmart chairman Gregory B Penner and the board demanding that former employees holding vested options not be disadvantaged or excluded from liquidity opportunities simply because they are no longer with the company. Over 30,000 current and former employees could potentially receive ₹38,000 crore from planned ESOP buybacks, with about half going to former workers. Signatories of the letter include Mukesh Bansal, Ankit Nagori, Amod Malviya, Ravi Garikipati, Mekin Maheshwari, and Anuj Chowdhary. The timeline for Flipkart's IPO remains uncertain.
